title: Client against server evaluation
summary: What EF Core cannot translate, the error you get, and how to move work to C# on purpose.

steps.title: When translation fails
body: EF Core translates what it understands. Call your own method inside a `Where`, and it has no idea what SQL that is:
```csharp fragment
static class Rules
public static bool IsLong(Book b) => b.Pages > 400;
db.Books.Where(b => Rules.IsLong(b)).ToList();     // compiles, but throws when it runs
```text
InvalidOperationException: The LINQ expression 'DbSet<Book>()
.Where(b => Rules.IsLong(b))' could not be translated. ...
Either rewrite the query in a form that can be translated, or switch to
client evaluation explicitly by inserting a call to 'AsEnumerable', ...
Old versions of EF quietly pulled **every row** into memory and filtered there. EF Core 3 made that an error on purpose: a query that worked on 100 test rows would melt on 10 million in production.
Fix it by writing the condition in translatable terms (`b.Pages > 400`), or, if you really mean to, bring rows to C# first.

code: var leGuin = new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Country = "US" };
var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },
new Book { Title = "Persuasion", Year = 1817, Pages = 249, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen });
public static bool IsLong(Book b) => b.Pages > 400;
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: EF Core cannot see inside `Rules.IsLong`, so the first query throws when it runs. Written as `b.Pages > 400`, the same rule becomes SQL and counts Dune and Emma.

steps.title: Client evaluation in the final Select
body: There is one place where EF Core **does** run your C#: the **last** `Select`. It fetches the columns your method needs and calls the method on each row as it arrives:
```csharp fragment
var labels = db.Books
.Where(b => b.Year > 1900)                       // SQL
.Select(b => Labels.Format(b.Title, b.Year))     // SQL reads Title, Year; Format runs in C#
.ToList();
static class Labels
public static string Format(string title, int year) => $"{title} ({year})";
That is safe: filtering already happened in the database, and the method only shapes each result.
To run the rest of a query in memory on purpose, switch with `AsEnumerable()`: everything before it is SQL, everything after is LINQ to Objects.
```csharp fragment
db.Books.Where(b => b.Genre == "Classic")     // SQL narrows the rows first
.AsEnumerable()
.Where(b => Rules.IsLong(b))              // then C#, on the few rows left

code: var leGuin = new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Country = "US" };
var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },
new Book { Title = "Persuasion", Year = 1817, Pages = 249, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen });
public static string Shout(string s) => s.ToUpper() + "!";
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: `Text.Shout` cannot be translated, but it is in the final `Select`, so EF Core reads `Title` in SQL and calls `Text.Shout` in C# on each row.

steps.prompt: Runs in the database, or in your program?
steps.explain: Everything on the `IQueryable` translates to SQL. Your own methods in the final projection, and anything after `AsEnumerable()` or `ToList()`, run in C#.

steps.prompt: A colleague fixes a translation error by putting `.ToList()` right after `db.Orders`, before a `Where`. Why is that dangerous?
options: It loads every order in the table into memory, then filters in C#
It makes the query run twice
steps.explain: It compiles and works on a small test database. In production it reads the entire table on every call. Narrow with translatable conditions first, then switch to C# for what is left.

steps.prompt: Filter in SQL first, then apply the C# rule on the rows that are left.
steps.explain: The year filter becomes SQL. `AsEnumerable()` switches to LINQ to Objects, so `Rules.IsLong` runs in C#, on only the books that survived the SQL filter.

steps.title: Fix the query
prompt: This method throws *could not be translated*. Rewrite it so **all** of the filtering and sorting runs in SQL, keeping only the final formatting (`Rules.Label`) in C#. Do not change what it returns.
The model is the usual one:
class Author { int Id; string Name; string Country; List<Book> Books; }
class Book   { int Id; string Title; int Year; int Pages; string Genre; int AuthorId; Author Author; }

The tests fill it with five books: Earthsea (Le Guin, 1968, 183 pages, Fantasy), The Dispossessed (Le Guin, 1974, 387, SciFi), Dune (Herbert, 1965, 412, SciFi), Emma (Austen, 1815, 474, Classic) and Persuasion (Austen, 1817, 249, Classic). Le Guin and Herbert are from the US, Austen from the UK.
starter: public static bool IsRecent(Book b) => b.Year >= 1960;
public static string SortKey(Book b) => b.Title.ToLower();
public static string Label(string title, int pages) => $"{title} [{pages}p]";
solution: public static string Label(string title, int pages) => $"{title} [{pages}p]";
template: var leGuin = new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Country = "US" };
var herbert = new Author { Name = "Herbert", Country = "US" };
var austen = new Author { Name = "Austen", Country = "UK" };
new Book { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Pages = 183, Genre = "Fantasy", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Pages = 387, Genre = "SciFi", Author = leGuin },
new Book { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Pages = 412, Genre = "SciFi", Author = herbert },
new Book { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Pages = 474, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen },
new Book { Title = "Persuasion", Year = 1817, Pages = 249, Genre = "Classic", Author = austen });
Dojo.Eq("the picks", new List<string> { "Dune [412p]", "Earthsea [183p]", "The Dispossessed [387p]" }, Picks(dojoDb));
Dojo.Check("filters in SQL", LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("WHERE") && LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("1960"), LibraryDb.LastSql);
Dojo.Check("sorts in SQL", LibraryDb.LastSql.Contains("ORDER BY lower("), LibraryDb.LastSql);
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;

protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=picks.db").LogTo((id, level) => id == RelationalEventId.CommandExecuted, e => { Commands++; LastSql = ((CommandExecutedEventData)e).Command.CommandText; });

forbid.message: Does not pull rows into memory early

hints: Inline the bodies of `IsRecent` and `SortKey` into the lambdas.
`Rules.Label` may stay: it is in the final `Select`.
